title: Your AI Coding Agent Just Leaked a Secret. Bots Found It on Docker Hub in 8 Seconds
content_md: TL;DR Bots read your Docker layers in 7.86 seconds : Stony Brook researchers planted keys in 300 honeypot images. Every AWS key was used within 15 minutes, and the median first API call came after 51 seconds. Your AI agent's memory ships with your code : Claude Code saves "don't ask again" commands, API keys included, to settings.local.json. GitGuardian found 31,088 distinct secrets in these files on GitHub, and a .gitignore will not keep them out of an image. Five fixes you can start today : Rotate what those files held, update .dockerignore, scan every layer, and stop the leak at the agent with AI Hooks. See what to do before the next bot gets there first. On Nov. 17, BleepingComputer reported on research from Billy Tsouvalas and Nick Nikiforakis of Stony Brook University. They published 300 honeypot images across eight public registries over four months and presented the findings at the most recent ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security earlier this month. The fastest planted AWS key was used 7.86 seconds after its image went live. That is far faster than any human or team could ever react. Developers commonly run AI coding agents, which make the same mistakes humans have been making for years: writing plaintext credentials into project config files. Those files follow the code into container builds. That is how Docker Hub secrets end up in front of the bots reading image layers.
